verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron: 📜
“If someone has a swelling, scab, or bright spot on their skin that may be a serious skin disease, bring them to Aaron the priest or one of his priestly sons. 🩺

“The priest must check the skin. If the hair in the spot has turned white and it looks deeper than the surrounding skin, it’s a skin disease. The priest must inspect the person and declare them unclean. 🔍
“If the bright spot is white but not deeper than the skin, and its hair hasn’t turned white, the priest must keep the person apart for seven days. 🗓️
“On day seven the priest must check again. If the spot hasn’t spread and looks unchanged, keep the person apart for seven more days. 🗓️
“On the seventh day, check again. If the spot has faded and hasn’t spread, the priest may declare the person clean; it’s only a scab. They must wash their clothes and will be clean. 🧼
“But if the scab spreads after the person has shown up to be declared clean, they must go back to the priest. 🔍
“The priest must inspect it. If the scab has spread, he must declare the person unclean; it’s a skin disease. ⚠️
“When someone has a skin disease, bring them to the priest. 🩺
“If the priest sees a white swelling, white hair, and raw flesh in the swelling, 🔍
“it’s a chronic skin disease. The priest must declare the person unclean right away; there’s no need to keep them apart. ⚠️
“If the disease breaks out across the skin and covers the person from head to toe, as far as the priest can see, 🩺
“the priest must examine them. If the disease has covered the whole body and turned all the skin white, he may declare them clean. ⚪
“But whenever raw flesh appears, the person is unclean. ⚠️
“The priest must inspect the raw flesh and declare the person unclean. Raw flesh means they’re unclean; it’s a skin disease. 🔍
“But if the raw flesh changes back to white, the person must go to the priest. ⚪
“The priest must examine them. If the spot has turned white, he may declare them clean; they are clean. 🔍
“If someone had a boil on their skin and it healed, 🩹
“but a white swelling or reddish-white spot shows up where the boil was, take it to the priest. 🔍
“If it looks deeper than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest must declare the person unclean. It’s a skin disease breaking out in the healed boil. ⚠️
“But if the priest sees no white hair, it isn’t deeper than the skin, and it has faded, keep the person apart for seven days. 🗓️
“If it spreads across the skin, the priest must declare the person unclean. It’s a disease. ⚠️
“If the spot stays put and doesn’t spread, it’s just the boil’s scar. The priest may declare the person clean. 🩹
“If someone gets burned by fire and raw flesh turns into a reddish-white or white spot, 🔥

“the priest must inspect it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot looks deeper than the skin, it’s a skin disease breaking out in the burn. The priest must declare the person unclean. 🔍
“But if the priest sees no white hair, the spot isn’t deeper than the skin, and it has faded, keep the person apart for seven days. 🗓️
“On day seven, the priest must inspect it. If the spot has spread across the skin, he must declare the person unclean; it’s a skin disease. 🔍
“If the spot stays put and hasn’t spread, but has faded, it’s only swelling from the burn. The priest may declare the person clean; it’s just the burn’s scar. 🩹
“If a man or woman has a sore on the head or beard, 🧑
“The priest must inspect it. If it looks deeper than the skin and the hair in it is thin and yellow, the priest must declare them unclean. It’s an itching disease of the head or beard. 🔍
“If the priest checks the itchy spot and it isn’t deeper than the skin, with no black hair in it, keep the person apart for seven days. 🗓️
“On day seven, check the sore. If it hasn’t spread, has no yellow hair, and isn’t deeper than the skin, 🔍
“shave the person’s hair—but not the affected spot—and keep them apart for seven more days. ✂️
“On the seventh day, check the sore again. If it hasn’t spread and isn’t deeper than the skin, the priest may declare the person clean. They must wash their clothes and will be clean. 🧼
“But if the sore spreads across the skin after they’ve been declared clean, ⚠️
“the priest must check them. If it has spread, don’t bother looking for yellow hair; the person is unclean. 🔍
“But if the sore has stopped spreading and black hair has grown in it, the sore has healed. The person is clean, and the priest must declare them clean. ✅
“If a man or woman has white spots on their skin, ⚪
“the priest must check them. If the spots are dull white, it’s only a harmless rash. The person is clean. 🔍
“If a man’s hair falls out on top, he’s bald but clean. 🧑‍🦲
“If his hair falls out at the front, his forehead is bald, but he’s still clean. 🧑‍🦲
“But if a reddish-white sore shows up on his bald scalp or forehead, a skin disease is breaking out there. ⚠️
“The priest must inspect him. If the swelling on his bald scalp or forehead is reddish-white, like a skin disease elsewhere on the body, 🔍
“he has a skin disease and is unclean. The priest must declare him unclean; the disease is on his head. ⚠️
“Anyone with the disease must wear torn clothes, let their hair hang loose, cover their upper lip, and call out, ‘Unclean! Unclean!’ 📣
“They remain unclean for as long as the disease lasts. They must live alone, outside the camp. 🏕️
“If mildew shows up in clothing—whether wool or linen—🧥
“in the lengthwise or crosswise threads of linen or wool, or in leather or any leather item; 🧶
“if the spot is greenish or reddish on fabric, leather, threads, or any leather item, it’s a mildew outbreak. Show it to the priest. 🟢
“The priest must inspect it and keep the item apart for seven days. 🗓️
“On day seven, inspect it again. If mildew has spread through the fabric, threads, or leather item—whatever it’s used for—it’s destructive mildew and unclean. ⚠️
“Burn the item—wool, linen, woven threads, or leather—because it’s destructive mildew. 🔥
“If the priest checks and mildew hasn’t spread in the fabric, threads, or leather, 🔍
“he must order the affected item to be washed and keep it apart for seven more days. 🧼

“After it’s washed, the priest must inspect it. If the color hasn’t changed and it hasn’t spread, the item is still unclean. Burn it in the fire; it’s mildew whether the bare patch is inside or outside. 🔥
“If the priest sees that the spot faded after washing, tear that patch out of the garment, leather, or threads. ✂️
“If it shows up again in the fabric, threads, or leather, it’s spreading. Burn the affected item in the fire. 🔥
“If washing makes the spot disappear from the garment, threads, or leather, wash it a second time and it will be clean.” 🧼
That’s the rule for mildew in wool or linen garments, woven threads, or leather items—for deciding whether they’re clean or unclean. 📜
